item.title: NFL Thanksgiving bold predictions: Packers vs. Rams must-win matchup, Lions & Bills defenses get tested
item.description: Subscribe to Football 301 with Nate Tice Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Nate Tice & Frank Schwab join forces to preview all five mid-week NFL Thanksgiving matchups. After airing out their thoughts on the Washington Commanders’ last-second win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night, the duo dive into the Green Bay Packers battling the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. With both teams’ playoff odds hanging in the balance, expect a kitchen sink matchup that should be a great appetizer for the rest of the Thanksgiving slate. Nate & Frank move on to the three Turkey Day matchups, including the Detroit Lions defense getting a true test in Caleb Williams & the Chicago Bears, the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles battling to stay relevant in the NFC East race and the Kansas City Chiefs giving the improving Buffalo Bills defense their toughest test of the season. The guys wrap things up with expectations for a Black Friday rock fight featuring the Denver Broncos & Pittsburgh Steelers. item.title: Kyle DeVan’s Intensity Drives Bears Offensive Line Success
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears offensive line found its voice not with a cheer, but with a scowl. After a win against the New England Patriots, assistant coach Kyle DeVan looked like someone had shot his dog, according to reports. This was not a moment of celebration for the 41-year-old coach, even though the team won from start to finish on a short week. DeVan explained his reaction with brutal honesty, stating, “I want to win every game and I want us to play the best we can, and when we don’t, I get a little not happy,” per the Chicago Tribune . That specific intensity is now the fuel the Bears are betting on to fix their line issues. Johnson’s Deliberate Plan Head coach Ben Johnson did not stumble into this pairing by accident. The Bears constructed Johnson’s first staff in February 2025 with a clear goal: find a younger assistant to work in tandem with veteran Dan Roushar. Johnson wants to develop young draft picks like Luke Newman into future starters once veterans move on. He openly admits that he drops DeVan’s name regularly on purpose to get him noticed by other teams. “I’m glad you caught that,” Johnson said of his references to DeVan, noting that the spotlight is by intent, per the Chicago Tribune. This strategy helps DeVan grow while keeping the Bears’ development pipeline strong. Strength in the Trenches The physical preparation for this line goes beyond just blocking schemes. Assistant strength and conditioning coach Mark Philippi brings a unique background that has the internet buzzing. A former world champion powerlifter, Philippi has qualified for the World’s Strongest Man competition seven times. Christian D’Andrea of For The Win joked that Philippi is the “final boss all other strength coaches must strive to defeat,” according to Sports Illustrated . Some fans even suggested the team should “suit up Mark Philippi” to solve their offensive line problems. Philippi’s presence ensures the players have the raw power to match DeVan’s technical demands. A Lesson in Celebration DeVan eventually learned that a win is hard to do and deserves a moment of joy. After being fined $100 by his linemen for his lack of celebration, he adjusted his approach. “I learned my lesson,” DeVan said. “I celebrate everything. I’ve been in this thing. A win is hard to do,” per the Chicago Tribune. This shift shows a coach who cares deeply about the process but respects the final result. The Bears face a tough test on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Ford Field against the Detroit Lions.

item.title: How Micah Ford flipped ignominious era for Stanford football into his personal legacy
item.description: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. item.title: MLB Pitch-Rigging Case Turns to Shocking Personal Texts
item.description: Jul 26, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Cleveland Guardians relief pitcher Emmanuel Clase (48) delivers a pitch against the Kansas City Royals in the ninth inning at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The federal trial of former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz continues this week in Brooklyn, with testimony focusing on the two June 2025 pitches prosecutors say Ortiz deliberately threw outside the strike zone in exchange for payments. Jurors have heard from a FanDuel executive that six wagers on Ortiz’s first pitch of the third inning on June 27 against the Cardinals generated more than $19,000 in winnings and led the sportsbook to suspend four accounts the next day. Those same accounts had also placed bets on an Ortiz pitch from June 15. Prosecutors argue those flagged bets helped launch the broader investigation. A cooperating witness, Enthony Diaz, has testified that he netted more than $31,000 on wagers tied to the two pitches Ortiz is accused of rigging. On the same June 27 date, prosecutors introduced WhatsApp messages between Ortiz and his wife that included the lines “Delete the evidence,” “What if he’s undercover?” and “Luis, it’s your future.” Ortiz has pleaded not guilty. His defense maintains he never communicated with the bettors and that the government’s case against him is thin. Clase, the former All-Star closer, is accused of providing information on roughly 18 pitches across three seasons (beginning in 2023) and recruiting Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Both players face charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, honest-services wire fraud, sports bribery, and money laundering. They remain on unpaid leave from the Guardians and are considered highly unlikely to pitch in the majors again regardless of the trial outcome. Prosecutors have indicated they expect to rest their case around Thanksgiving, with closing arguments and a possible verdict in early December. MLB continues its own investigation parallel to the criminal proceedings.

item.title: Brazil U17's Kauê Furquim named man of the match v Tanzania, thanks team
item.description: Brazil U17's Kauê Furquim named man of the match v Tanzania, thanks team Number 7 named player of the match in win over Tanzania Credits: Handout /CBF Named player of the match in Brazil’s 1-0 win over Tanzania on Tuesday (24) at the U-17 World Cup, Kauê Furquim celebrated the individual recognition and shared the credit with his national team teammates, the coaching staff and his family. The forward also spoke about the importance of staying focused as the competition progresses. “First of all, I want to thank God, the national team and everyone in our squad. Without them, I wouldn’t have achieved this. I also want to thank my family and all my staff. I’m very happy to have won this award,” said the Bahia forward. Kauê also celebrated the result and Brazil’s qualification for the second round of the World Cup with a game to spare. Despite having secured their place, the player stressed that the team still has goals to achieve in the group stage. “I’m very happy. Thank God we managed to qualify after our second game, but we still have one last match. We’re preparing for that game so we can finish top of the group,” he said. The forward also noted that the standard of the competition demands focus and commitment in every match. In his view, the national team must keep their feet on the ground and keep working to achieve their ultimate goal. “Every game will be a final. There won’t be any easy games for us. That’s why we have to keep working, with our feet firmly on the ground, to reach our ultimate goal,” he added. With two wins in two games, Brazil reached six points and secured qualification with a match to spare. The national team wraps up its group-stage campaign against Costa Rica on Friday (27), seeking another positive result to finish top of Group I. item.title: Veteran quarterback among Tigers to know for Alabama vs. Auburn
item.description: Entering the final week of the regular season, only one team stands between Alabama and a College Football Playoff berth, the Auburn Tigers. One of college football's greatest rivalries, the Iron Bowl has a lengthy history that dates back to the late 1800's, and is a matchup which Alabama has owned in recent years. The Crimson Tide have won the last six games between the two since 2020, as well as the last three played in Tuscaloosa. This latest Iron Bowl matchup will be Kalen DeBoer's third since arriving in Tuscaloosa, with Alabama's roster led by a number of players who have seen action against the Tigers before such as Ryan Coleman-Williams, Zabien Brown, and Bray Hubbard, among others. Auburn's roster though is a mixture of players which Alabama faced a year ago, as well as numerous new faces at a few key positions. Many of these came from USF where they followed head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn this past offseason, a nonconference team that Alabama has faced twice in recent years. Here are five Tigers to know ahead of the Saturday's Iron Bowl , as well as how each has performed against Alabama before. Byrum Brown, Quarterback The USF transfer is in his first season as Auburn's starting quarterback completing 65.6% of passes for 2,035 yards and a 15:8 TD:INT ratio, while also leading the Tigers in rushing with 644 yards and nine scores on 177 attempts. As a result of his time at USF, the fifth-year senior has faced Alabama twice before in 2023-24 completing a combined 29-of-63 (46%) passes for 190 yards and one interception. Brown also rushed for 200 yards on 46 attempts during those two prior matchups. Keshaun Singleton, Wide Receiver Singleton is another USF transfer who currently leads Auburn in receiving this season with 58 catches for 744 yards and eight touchdowns. The senior did not record any stats against the Crimson Tide in 2024 while at USF. Chas Nimrod, Wide Receiver Nimrod is yet another USF transfer who sits just behind Singleton in receiving this season with 51 receptions for 638 yards and seven touchdowns. The fifth-year senior has faced Alabama twice before while at Tennessee in 2023-24, but did not record any stats in either game. Elijah Melendez, Linebacker The arguable leader of Auburn's defense is Melendez, a sophomore linebacker who leads the team with 74 tackles, 49 of which have been solo. Melendez also has 10 TFL, four sacks, one interception, and six pass defenses so far this season, and will be facing Alabama for the second time after recording one tackle a year ago in Auburn. Jeremiah Cobb, Running Back Auburn's top running back is Cobb, a senior who has 101 carries for 566 yards and four touchdowns this season, as well as 16 receptions for 141 yards and another score. This will be the running back's fourth-career meeting against Alabama, with Cobb having rushed for 33 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries a year ago. item.title: Yaya on Brazil's mood and why friendlies matter for the World Cup
item.description: Yaya on Brazil's mood and why friendlies matter for the World Cup The second player to arrive in Hiroshima, Japan, midfielder Vitória Yaya spoke about her expectations for Brazil’s final fixtures of 2026. Called up for the two friendlies against Japan, the Paris Saint-Germain player discussed what it feels like to reunite with her Brazil teammates and how the atmosphere differs from everyday life at her club. “Getting together with the girls on the national team is incredible; it’s a completely different atmosphere. We know each other and share that Brazilian spirit, which is something I miss a little over there (at the club). It’s always great to be around people from Brazil, and it does me good,” she said. Looking ahead to the matches against Japan, the midfielder emphasized how challenging the games would be and the opportunity to face a team with unique qualities. Yaya also highlighted the importance of playing against national teams with different styles during this World Cup preparation cycle, as Brazil do not yet know who their opponents will be in the tournament. “I believe these two matches will teach us a lot and be very difficult. Brazil’s main challenge will be man-to-man marking because Japan are a team that moves around a lot, but we’ll be ready for that.” “It’s always good to prepare by playing strong teams, and considering we still don’t know our World Cup opponents, having faced a variety of opponents will be very good for us,” she concluded. Brazil’s women’s national team will face Japan twice. The first friendly will take place on Sunday (29) at 1:55 a.m. (Brasília time) at Edion Peace Wing Stadium in Hiroshima. The second match is scheduled for December 5 at 3 a.m. (Brasília time) at JFE Harenokuni Stadium in Okayama. item.title: Wickens Full IMSA Season With Hanley Motorsports Is A Win For Racing
item.description: Racing driver Robert Wickens congratulates Meyer Shank Racing with Curb Agajanian driver Felix Rosenqvist (60) after the 110th running of the Indianapolis 500 on Sunday, May 24, 2026, at Indianapolis Motor Speedway. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Starting in 2027, Robert Wickens is set to compete across a full season within the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. He teams up with Mason Filippi for Hanley Motorsports in the GTD class. This marks the first time the Canadian driver competes in every race of the series. The #42 BMW M4 GT3 EVO will be shared by the pair for the new Georgia-based team. The announcement came on Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. It confirms what many fans expected after the duo raced together in sprint rounds this year. Motorsport.com reported the signing details and the specific car model they will use. Wickens shifts from partial schedules to a full campaign. It also gives the new team a strong starting lineup for its debut year. A Custom Machine For A Top Driver The #42 car features a special setup designed for Wickens’ needs. Bosch will install modified hand controls and an electronic braking system. This tech was first built for his Corvette in 2024 and now moves to the BMW. The system allows him to race at the highest level despite his spinal cord injury from 2018. Wickens has a history of success with these tools. He earned five top-10 finishes in 2025 and 2026 while driving for DXDT Racing. He also grabbed his first career IMSA GTD pole at Long Beach in 2026. He is not just a participant; he is a former Formula One test driver and a 2018 IndyCar Rookie of the Year. His return to full-time racing validates years of hard work. Wickens expressed his feelings about the deal in a statement released on Tuesday. “I’ve worked incredibly hard for a long time to reach this point in my career, and I’m filled with gratitude for everyone who has helped me achieve my goal of returning to the highest levels of motorsports,” Wickens said. He also noted his excitement to build on the strengths he has developed with Filippi. A Proven Partner In Filippi Mason Filippi brings a winning record to the partnership. He just won the 2026 IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge TCR class championship. His season included three wins and eight podiums. In the WeatherTech Championship last season, he recorded six top-10 finishes. He capped that effort with a podium at the Motul Petit Le Mans finale at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta. The two drivers already know how to work together. R. Sportscar365 noted that their combination was widely expected since August. They have a great relationship and have accomplished a lot in a short time. Filippi called the move a dream come true for him. “I couldn’t be more excited for the opportunity to be part of HMI,” Filippi said. item.title: Bills-Chiefs showdown tops NFL Thanksgiving holiday slate
item.description: Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes, left, and Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, right, will lead their clubs into an NFL Thanksgiving holiday showdown with the best record in the NFL's American Conference up for grabs (David Eulitt) Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Buffalo superstar Josh Allen face a Thursday showdown on the US Thanksgiving holiday that will have a major impact on the NFL playoff picture. The Bills own the AFC's best record at 9-1 and beating the Chiefs (8-2) would help ensure a home-field edge in the post-season. "We know what type of team they are," Allen said. "They've been one of the best teams in the league the last 10 years. So, you've got to play your best." Mahomes, whose club shares the AFC West division lead with Denver, hopes to snap Buffalo's six-game win streak. "It will be a great challenge for us. We're excited for it," Mahomes said. "You know it's going to take your best football. "Every time we play each other, it always comes down to the end of the game. It's about who makes the big plays in the big moments. It's always exciting. It's always fun." The Bills have averaged 31 points in their win streak while the Chiefs have won three in a row with 34 or more points each game. Allen's Bills and Mahomes's Chiefs are 5-5 in all-time meetings, but it's not so even when it comes to realizing and crushing title hopes. Allen and the Bills are 5-1 in regular-season matchups against Kansas City but Mahomes and the Chiefs are 4-0 in playoff games against Buffalo. The Chiefs have won three Super Bowls and lost two others in the past seven seasons while the Bills have not reached the Super Bowl since losing four in a row from 1991-1994 and were eliminated from the playoffs by Kansas City in four of the past six seasons. "It's the most important one because it's the next one," Allen said of the game. "All the seeding implications, that is what it is. We're just trying to find a way to go 1-0 each week." Cold, windy and rainy conditions are forecast for the contest. "I take pride in being able to throw the ball in any conditions," Mahomes said. The Bills-Chiefs contest tops five games to be played around the US Thanksgiving holiday. Green Bay will visit the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday in a matchup of 6-4 clubs while Thursday also sees Philadelphia at Dallas and a showdown for the NFC North lead when Chicago visits Detroit. Both are 8-2 with the Bears having won five games in a row and Detroit's streak at six. Denver (8-2) carries a six-game win streak into Pittsburgh (6-4) on Friday. - Respect for Allen - Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo respects Allen's poise as well as passing and rushing skills. "You're hoping somewhere along the way he makes a mistake. When he plays (us), it seems like he's on fire and becomes Superman. Somehow we've got to force him into a bad throw," he said. item.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' executive producers talk architectural easter eggs and franchise continuity for Prime Video's new sci-fi series (interview)
item.description: null Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. Here, Yeoh's dying replicant blade runner Olwen unites with Schafer’s Cora, a human masquerading as a synthetic, to hunt down a dangerous rogue replicant that holds the key to a dark secret. (Image credit: Alberto Rodriguez/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) We spoke to Kosove and Johnson about being respectful keepers of "Blade Runner's" creative flame, the pitch that sold them, and dipping back into Dick's original novel. "When the original film came out in 1982, and even when "2049" came out about a decade ago, a lot of things that these movies envisioned seemed far, far away and hard to comprehend," Kosovo tells Space. "The creation of artificial sentient beings. Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner,' with artificial technology and concerns of how do humans use this technology for our benefit without it taking over." "Silka came in several years ago and pitched her very simple idea, which was, the next chapter of 'Blade Runner' should be what happens when the replicants overtake their creators." explains Kosovo. "We thought that idea was going to be particularly resonant. It was simple to understand so new fans could enter the world without being steeped in the first two movies. And we thought it had logical continuity to the story canon that came before it. It checked a number of key boxes for us. Even though we talked to a number of showrunners who were much more established in their careers than Silka was at that point, she won the day with the most elegant idea in our opinion." (Image credit: Prime Video) Johnson admits that Louisa's pitch approval was just the opening round of a multitude of responsible decisions to be ruminated over as the production process advanced. "Once you agree that this is the story we’re telling, then it becomes a multi-year partnership in honoring all the artists and visionaries that came before as it relates to visual design and music," he notes. item.title: NC State football adds former NFL wide receiver to coaching staff
item.description: Bob Donnan-USA TODAY Sports NC State football adds former NFL wide receiver to coaching staff appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the NC State football program hiring former quarterback Philip Rivers as its next head coach, he has been building up his staff, with the latest move coming on the offensive side of the ball. As Rivers and the NC State football program hired Jason Michael as its offensive coordinator , the team has found its wide receivers coach, as it’s a familiar name for the school. According to college football insider Pete Nakos at On3 Sports, the Wolfpack has brought in Jerricho Cotchery as their wide receivers coach, as he played the position with NC State and in the NFL. Rivers is no doubt familiar with Cotchery, as the two were on the Wolfpack, and the receivers were the top target for the quarterback, with the reunion at the university happening once again, but this time in coaching. “NC State has hired former Wolfpack and NFL wide receiver Jerricho Cotchery as its wide receivers coach,” Nakos wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “He was a top target of Philip Rivers in college and will now be on his staff. He’s been the assistant head coach and passing game coordinator for North Greenville.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cotchery will join Michael’s offensive staff, as Nakos reported that hire last Wednesday. “Philip Rivers and NC State have hired former Eagles assistant Jason Michael as offensive coordinator,” Nakos wrote. More on Philip Rivers being the next NC State football head coach There’s no denying that the hiring of Rivers to the NC State football program is a thrilling one for fans and the college football world, though some could be concerned about the lack of head coaching experience. The only head coaching role under his belt is for St. Michael Catholic HS in Fairhope, Alabama. “I wasn’t always around there, but I was always pulling for the Pack, ” Rivers said to Pat McAfee on his self-titled show. “There is no place in college football that would have been intriguing for me. This is home.” “I’m fired up to be leading the Pack,” Rivers continued. “There’s no place in college football that would’ve even been intriguing at all for me. This is home.” —Philip Rivers on coming back to NC State as head coach 🥹 (via @PatMcAfeeShow ) pic.twitter.com/YcKfwhrsTz — ESPN College Football (@ESPNCFB) November 17, 2026 At any rate, Rivers will continue building his Wolfpack staff as the offseason continues. item.title: Steelers urged to extend key offensive player before it's too late
item.description: Steelers urged to extend key offensive player before it's too late originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming up on a big game against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, and it's shaping up to be a real watch. The Broncos are 8-2 heading into the matchup, and the Steelers are 6-4, so it's a critical game for two franchises hoping to go deep in the playoffs. But the powers that be should also be looking toward the future of this franchise. They have one player on their roster that they're being urged to extend as soon as possible. ESPN believes the Steelers should prioritize a contract extension for Zach Frazier In a piece released on Tuesday discussing all of the NFL teams heading into Week 12 , ESPN's Brooke Pryor urges the team to extend center Zach Frazier. She says he's basically proven himself. "Frazier has shown the makings of a long-term anchor for the group throughout his three seasons as a starter; quarterback Aaron Rodgers has frequently praised the center's intelligence," she notes. "Extension eligible for the first time this offseason, the 2024 second-round pick has played a big role in the Steelers' offensive line renovation." She adds, "Not only are they likely to prioritize extending him because they believe in building through the trenches, Frazier also figures to be an invaluable resource for the team's next starting quarterback -- a player who will have much less experience than Rodgers." With Rodgers retiring after this year, it really does make extending Frazier's deal even more important. They need some consistency on offense. Losing Rodgers is going to be a big blow, and having a reliable player like Frazier who knows the drill will be invaluable. item.title: Sidney Crosby wants to be a ‘Penguin forever’, agent claims
item.description: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Sidney Crosby wants to be a ‘Penguin forever’, agent claims appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Penguins are mired in a disappointing season so far in the NHL. Pittsburgh has reportedly been considering moving Sidney Crosby , ahead of the league’s trade deadline. Crosby’s agent is now throwing cold water on that idea. “His goal is to be a Penguin forever,” Crosby’s agent Pat Brisson said, per Sportsnet. Crosby has played his entire NHL career in Pittsburgh. He is a fan-favorite in that city, and has helped lead the Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In prior comments, Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas appeared to be on the same page as Crosby. “In Sid’s case, he’s as unique as it gets,” Dubas said recently, per NHL.com. “I would just go back to my view on it from the opening of the season, is that we want to get into this (season) as far as we can, have an indication about where we’re at and where we’re going, and make sure everyone’s comfortable with that. And then, he’s owed all the respect in the world. “If he wants to be here, that’s great, and that’s obviously what we would love as well.” Crosby is clearly closing in on the end of his legendary career. This season, his production has been down. Crosby has 15 points this season in 23 games. “Crosby is in the final season of a two-year, $17.4-million contract and can become an unrestricted free agent following the 2026-27 campaign. He also holds a full no-movement clause, giving him control over any potential trade destination,” Sportsnet reported. The Penguins have just 16 points on the campaign . Pittsburgh is currently last in points in the Eastern Conference. This isn’t the way it was supposed to go this year, as the Penguins made the Stanley Cup Playoffs during the 2025-26 season. Pittsburgh next plays the Calgary Flames on Wednesday. The NHL trade deadline this season is on March 1. MORE PITTSBURGH PENGUINS NEWS NHL rumors: Rickard Rakell’s Blackhawks trade rejection leads to existential crisis

item.title: Why Yankees didn't match Cubs' $120 million offer to Teruaki Sato
item.description: Why Yankees didn't match Cubs' $120 million offer to Teruaki Sato originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees were reportedly involved in the sweepstakes for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato. However, the former Hanshin Tigers star signed a six-year, $120 million contract with the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday, ESPN's Jeff Passan reports. "BREAKING: Two-time Central League MVP Teruaki Sato and the Chicago Cubs are in agreement on a six-year, $120 million contract, sources tell ESPN," Passan reports. While the Yankees are looking for a third base upgrade, Sato is now off the market. At some point, the AL East club likely bowed out of the race for the third baseman and corner outfielder due to his price tag. The Athletic's Brendan Kuty reports the Yankees weren't comfortable giving Sato the $120 million the Cubs offered the left-handed hitter. "To clarify: Out of budget for what they may have been willing to spend on Sato," Kuty wrote on X. To clarify: Out of budget for what they may have been willing to spend on Sato. League source says Yankees are in on Adrian Morejon, though unclear where things stand currently in talks for the LHP. They’re far from the only team, but he makes a lot of sense for the Yankees. — Brendan Kuty 🧟‍♂️ (@BrendanKutyNJ) November 24, 2026 Since the Yankees usually have one of the highest payrolls in the Majors, Sato was not out of their price range. Still, it sounds like they were unwilling to give him the deal, perhaps both years and money, the Cubs were. MORE : Full contract details on Tarik Skubal’s reported $450M deal with Mets It probably wasn't a matter of affordability, but rather comfortability. Currently, New York's starting third baseman is Ryan McMahon, who had another season of below-average offensive production. Expect the Yankees to make at least one external addition for third base before next season begins, whenever that may be. item.title: Paul Pierce Admits 2013 Trade Built Current Celtics Core
item.description: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics won the 2024 NBA title, but the foundation was laid when the franchise traded away its biggest star. Paul Pierce, the man who led the team to victory in 2008, says he has zero regrets about leaving in 2013. He knows the picks Boston received from that deal turned into the two players who finally brought the trophy back. The Trade That Changed Everything Back in 2013, the Brooklyn Nets were desperate and desperate teams make mistakes. They traded for Pierce and Kevin Garnett, giving up three unprotected first-round picks and a pick swap. The Nets project failed hard, and the assets Boston got in return became the keys to the kingdom. According to HITC , Pierce told the Amongst Legends podcast that the trade was handled with total transparency. He respected the process even though it meant leaving Boston. When the Nets finished with a 21-61 record in 2016, Boston used the number three overall pick to draft Jaylen Brown. The next year, the Celtics exercised their pick swap after Brooklyn had the worst record in the league. In the 2017 Draft, Danny Ainge traded down to let the Sixers select Markelle Fultz while the Lakers chose Lonzo Ball. Boston then swooped in to select Jayson Tatum with the third pick. Those two young stars led the team to a championship in 2024, defeating the Mavericks in the Finals. Pierce Owns The Legacy Many fans might think trading Pierce was a mistake, but he sees it differently now. He says the current success of the franchise rests on the foundation his departure created. A Look Back at California Roots Conner Henry, a native of Claremont, California, is part of that long history. He was selected by the Houston Rockets in the 1988 NBA Draft, but he had signed with Boston in 1987. His time with the team was short, lasting only until he was cut that fall. During his stay, Henry averaged 2.7 points per game. AOL.com notes that the Celtics have sought talent from nearly every U.S. state since their early days.

item.title: Minnesota Wild Waive Veteran Goalie
item.description: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild have never had more points through 26 games than they do right now. Monday’s 5-2 win at San Jose moved them to 18-3-5 with 41 points, first in the NHL, and pushed their point streak to a franchise-record 15 games. That win was also Filip Gustavsson’s first regular-season start since April 13 and his first appearance of 2026-27. Last year’s starter stopped 22 of 24 shots in his return from long-term injured reserve . When the Wild activated him Monday, they placed Quinn Hughes on injured reserve. Putting Hughes on IR let Calvin Pickard stay on the roster for now, giving Minnesota three goalies on the active roster. Last night in San Jose, Pickard backed up Gustavsson while starter Jesper Wallstedt got the night off. Minnesota Wild place Calvin Pickard on waivers On Tuesday afternoon, however, the Minnesota Wild announced that Pickard has been placed on waivers, an inevitable move after Gus Bus came back. If Pickard clears, he will go to Iowa, which would open up $1 million in cap space for Minnesota. Given the desperation around the league for competent goaltender depth, it’s very plausible he doesn’t make it that far. The result should come Wednesday. Until then, he technically remains on Minnesota’s NHL roster. The #mnwild has placed goaltender Calvin Pickard on waivers. — Minnesota Wild PR (@mnwildPR) November 24, 2026 Related: Top MN Wild Insider Weighs in on Severity of Mysterious Hughes Injury Pickard has made three starts for the Wild this season, going 1-1-1 with a 3.60 goals-against average and an .855 save percentage. He lost Oct. 13 at Winnipeg, won Oct. 25 at Vancouver and took an overtime loss Nov. 7 against Tampa Bay. The 34-year-old from Moncton, New Brunswick, was a second-round pick by Colorado in 2010. He has also played for Toronto, Philadelphia, Arizona, Detroit and Edmonton. In his NHL career, Pickard is 75-78-15 with a 2.97 GAA, a .900 save percentage and five shutouts in 194 games . He also went 8-2 in 13 playoff games with Edmonton. What happens if Calvin Pickard clears waivers? Pickard has already said he’d be open to playing for AHL Iowa. In an interview this week , he praised Wallstedt and the Wild locker room. “I’ve been on good teams, but the culture here is second to none,” he said. Iowa’s roster currently lists two goalies, Riley Mercer and William Rousseau. Related: Reports: Injury to MN Wild Superstar Not Considered Serious Pickard signed a one-year, $1 million contract with Minnesota on July 1 . It’s a one-way deal that pays him $1 million in the NHL or the minors, and he will be an unrestricted free agent after this season. That cap hit is under this season’s burying threshold of $1,225,000, so the full $1 million would come off Minnesota’s cap if he’s assigned to Iowa. The Wild currently have $322,137 in cap space with a full 23-man roster. Read more at Minnesota Sports Fan

item.title: Van Malone, Hampton make huge staff shake-up following 1-11 season
item.description: © Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Van Malone, Hampton make huge staff shake-up following 1-11 season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a disappointing 1-11 season in his first campaign at Hampton University , Van Malone has made a major staff shakeup. Per a press release by the athletics department, Malone has dismissed five coaches and two support staff members. “As we prepare for 2027, we are aligning our staff with the work ahead and the direction of Hampton football,” said Malone in the statement. “I want to thank each of these staff members and their families for their time, care and commitment to Hampton football, and we wish them success in their next steps. Our focus is on preparing our student-athletes and building a team that represents Hampton well.” The list is below. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Name Title Dwyan Luckey Tight ends coach and special teams coordinator Kenny Ray Offensive line coach and run game coordinator Trevor Trout Defensive tackles coach Rick Purcell Linebackers coach Nescotia Harrison Director of football operations Jasmine Payne Assistant director of strength and conditioning Kawana Dios Santos Offensive graduate assistant In addition to the changes, Connor Looper was announced as moving from wide receivers coach to tight ends coach. Malone was hired to lead Hampton University football last December, following a stint at Kansas State as assistant head coach. Hampton’s only victory was in week one of the season against Virginia University of Lynchburg, 45-0. They then went on to lose 11 straight games, all by double figures. Malone looks to bring Hampton back to the prominence that they enjoyed in 2017 and 2018, the last two seasons that they had a winning record. In 2017, in their last year in the MEAC, they went 6-5. In 2018, they finished 7-3. 2018 is their last winning season. item.title: Dodgers Have New Plan for Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy After Royce Lewis Trade
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hope to rest two of their top players after trading for Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins. Why the Dodgers needed infield depth The Dodgers gave up Bobby Miller , who still has a good deal of team control, for Lewis, the former No. 1 overall pick and top prospect who fizzled out over the last three years after two strong first seasons. The Dodgers’ biggest strength, in terms of depth, is pitching, especially in the marginal parts of the roster, while the infield could use some work. Alex Freeland and Hyeseong Kim are the two younger options, though both have struggles with offense despite strong defense. Sep 15, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Twins first baseman Royce Lewis (23) celebrates his run against the New York Yankees in the second inning on a single by center fielder Emmanuel Rodriguez (not pictured) at Target Field. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tommy Edman has also struggled at the plate, while Kike Hernandez is a free agent and Miguel Rojas has retired. With so many moving pieces, the Dodgers went after the reclamation project in Lewis. What will Royce Lewis’ role be Now, Freddie Freeman and Max Muncy are in line for some rest, as long as Lewis performs well. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Katie Woo of The Athletic , in his latest report on the Dodgers’ plans, noted that rest days are important to the Dodgers’ roster building. “[Andrew] Friedman covets versatility. He also wants to incorporate some youth. Lewis, 27, played most of his games at first base last season, but over his five-year career he has played third base the most (239 games),” Woo wrote. “Lewis also has experience playing second base and shortstop. His flexibility should allow the Dodgers to spell Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman when needed, while moving Tommy Edman to a more traditional utility job in both the infield and outfield. “The Dodgers expect Alex Freeland to mix in, but adding Lewis gives them experience while ensuring rest days for other players.” Aug 25, 2026; West Sacramento, California, USA; Minnesota Twins first baseman Royce Lewis (23) fields a ground ball against the Athletics during the first inning at Sutter Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Muncy had a fantastic season, showing his best third-base defense and a Silver Slugger-caliber season, while Freeman struggled with a power drought, but his defense remained among the best as well. Hoping to get them through the season, the Dodgers will try to take them off their feet. Muncy has already been quiet receptive to getting rested, especially down the stretch, though Freeman is notorious for wanting to play every day. Getting a capable player is one challenge, but selling the plan to Freeman will be another. As one of the leaders on the team, if the Dodgers make a definitive call

item.title: Scottie Scheffler, Wyndham Clark headline PGA Tour Player of the Year finalists
item.description: Scottie Scheffler has another shot at PGA Tour Player of the Year, but he’ll have plenty of competition. Scheffler, Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young were named Tuesday as the five finalists for the Jack Nicklaus Award, given annually to the PGA Tour Player of the Year. The Tour also announced five finalists for the Arnold Palmer Award as Rookie of the Year: Alex Fitzpatrick, Ben James, Jackson Koivun, Marco Penge and Kristoffer Reitan. Scheffler’s case starts with another huge season. The world No. 1 won three times, including the season-ending Tour Championship, claimed the FedEx Cup and led the Tour with 13 top-10 finishes in 20 starts. He also won the Byron Nelson Award with a 68.619 scoring average and missed just one cut. Clark also won three times in 25 starts, highlighted by the U.S. Open , along with victories at the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and BMW Championship. He finished the season with six top-10s. Matt Fitzpatrick matched that three-win total, taking the Valspar Championship, RBC Heritage and Zurich Classic of New Orleans. He posted eight top-10s in 21 starts and missed just one cut. Gotterup also made it a three-win season, capturing the Sony Open in Hawaii, WM Phoenix Open and John Deere Classic. He finished No. 4 in the FedEx Cup and recorded seven top-10s in 23 starts. Young is the only Player of the Year finalist with just two victories, but one of them was a big one. He won the Players Championship and later added the Cadillac Championship, finished with eight top-10s and didn’t miss a cut in 20 starts. The Rookie of the Year race features a mix of winners and some of the game’s most recognizable young players. Alex Fitzpatrick won the Zurich Classic alongside his brother, Matt, to secure his Tour card. He then went on to record six top-10 finishes and was one of only two rookies to reach the Tour Championship, finishing No. 4 in the FedEx Cup. Koivun, one of the biggest names to arrive from the college game, won the 3M Open and added three more top-10 finishes. He qualified for the FedEx Cup Playoffs despite having just five regular-season starts and earned a captain's pick for the 2026 U.S. Presidents Cup team. Penge capped his rookie season with a victory at the RSM Classic this past weekend , while Reitan won the Truist Championship and joined Fitzpatrick as the only other rookie to qualify for the Tour Championship. James didn’t notch a win but came close several times. He had runner-up finishes at the Biltmore Championship Asheville and World Wide Technology Championship, along with three other top-five finishes. He made 12 cuts in 14 starts after earning his card as the No. 1 player in the 2026 PGA Tour University ranking. The winners will be determined by a vote of PGA Tour members who competed in at least 15 official events during the 2026 season. Voting closes Dec. 4 at 5 p.m. ET, with the winners to be announced later. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek. This article originall

item.title: Michigan State Fortunate in QB Transfer Outlook
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 07: Alessio Milivojevic #11 of the Michigan State Spartans throws a first half pass against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty MADISON, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 03: Alessio Milivojevic #11 of the Michigan State Spartans warms up prior to the game against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 04: Alessio Milivojevic #11 of the Michigan State Spartans plays against the Toledo Rockets at Spartan Stadium on September 04, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) In the modern world of college football, quarterback transfers are incredibly common — and for many, a great team-building opportunity. Michigan State could actually find itself in a more comfortable position than most of the Spartans’ competitors this offseason, though. At a time when most teams find themselves seeking a new QB in the portal, Michigan State may not have to. That’s not to say MSU won’t be active — there are a lot of holes to fill on the Spartans’ roster, and they’re unlikely to retain all the players currently in East Lansing, either. But at the most important position in sports, it appears Michigan State has a guy to feel good about in Alessio Milivojevic. Alessio Milivojevic Transfer Outlook Getty MADISON, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 03: Alessio Milivojevic #11 of the Michigan State Spartans warms up prior to the game against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) While things could clearly still change, at least at the moment, CBS Sports writer Brad Crawford shared in a new article on Tuesday that he expects Milivojevic to be the Spartans’ starter in 2027. The fit makes sense, and there’s not a ton of reason for Milivojevic to leave. “A captain this season for the Spartans under first-year coach Pat Fitzgerald, Milivojevic will be a fourth-year junior next season with 15 career starts under his belt,” Crawford writes. “While his numbers have been pedestrian compared to other QB1s in the Big Ten, some of that is due to Michigan State losing its top offensive playmaker, Nick Marsh, to Indiana in the portal and struggling to produce in the run game. For Milivojevic to thrive, the Spartans must be balanced and importantly, spend heavy on talent acquisition in a few weeks to give OC Nick Sheridan an opportunity to flex his pay-calling acumen next fall. The former college quarterback should get a career-best campaign out of Milivojevic with another year under his belt of development with the veteran.” Milivojevic won’t fully thrive until there’s a better roster around him, but he’s proven to be promising enough to stick with for another year. item.title: AFC North Contender Has ‘No Interest’ in Daniel Jones
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts calls a play against the Houston Texans during the first quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) Getty The Indianapolis Colts made the shocking decision to release Daniel Jones following last Thursday’s ugly loss in prime time. He entered the season on a brand new two-year, $88 million deal and was cut in Year 1 before Thanksgiving. That leaves the Colts in a state of limbo given the fact the team does not own a first-round pick in 2027. Jones is free to sign with any team and has been linked to a number of contenders by fans. However, the actual teams don’t seem to be in a rush to add his services. One AFC North contender in particular is reportedly not even remotely considering Jones. Insider Shuts Down Daniel Jones to Cleveland Mary Kay Cabot covers the Cleveland Browns for cleveland.com and recently shared a post on X ending any Jones to Cleveland rumors. “The Browns have no interest in signing QB Daniel Jones, who cleared waivers today after being released by the Colts,” she wrote. This comes at a time when the Browns are off to a 6-4 start with Deshaun Watson at quarterback. Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel sit behind him on the depth chart, leading some to think the Browns may want a veteran presence in the room. Instead, Todd Monken and his staff seem comfortable with the players they have as the Browns look to make the playoffs for the first time in three years. Jones Continues to Wait So where will the former Colts quarterback sign? The Browns were one intriguing option, as were the New England Patriots before head coach Mike Vrabel shut that down , at least for now. The Minnesota Vikings, one of Jones’ former teams, already found a replacement in Kirk Cousins. That leaves perhaps the Arizona Cardinals as the only QB-desperate team remaining after starting veteran journeyman Josh Johnson on Sunday. Yet that team may be content chasing a top pick and letting Carson Beck play when he is healthy. It’s entirely possible Jones takes the rest of the year off and enjoys his massive fortune from the Colts. However, there is still over a month left in the regular season and plenty can happen between now and Week 18. Any contending team that loses a quarterback to injury could be on the phone with Jones’ agent right away. That means the veteran can sit back and wait for the best possible opportunity, as opposed to joining a team with a losing record where he is not the future at the position. As for the Colts, the team is in a very weird spot at the moment. A number of key veterans were traded away at the deadline, Jones was cut, and Anthony Richardson is the new starting quarterback. Richardson, the former No. 4 overall pick, is a free agent after the season. Add in the fact head coach Shane Steichen will likely be fired and the Colts are in no man’s land heading into 2027. item.title: Browns' Raheim Sanders 'blessed' by 'opportunity' for practice return
item.description: BEREA ― Raheim "Rocket" Sanders couldn't hide the smile on his face as the prepared for practice inside the Browns ' locker room. The second-year running back remains on the injured reserve list due to a hip injury he sustained in Week 5 against the New York Jets. However, the Browns announced Nov. 24 they were opening up Sanders' 21-day window for return. "Man, I feel great," Sanders said. "Just blessed for the opportunity again and just got to take advantage of it just one day at a time for real." Subscribe to Browns Insider newsletter The Browns have until Dec. 14 to either put Sanders on the active roster or he'll stay on injured reserve for the remainder of the season. The routine when they have brought a player back from injured reserve has typically been one week of ramping up, then activated at the end of the second week of practice. For Sanders, if that was the case, he would likely still be out when the Browns (6-4) play the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football." However, that would put him on track to come back the next week when they play a critical AFC North game against the division-leading Cincinnati Bengals . While there's no definitive time Sanders will return, the fact he's back practice points to a return sooner rather than later. That's not a major surprise to him, even if there was some concern about the injury initially. "I'd definitely say from a standpoint of just how I take care of business, I feel like I would just be back," Sanders said. "But just like I said, taking it one day at a time." Sanders had 43 rushing yards on nine carries at the time of the injury, which came in the second half against the Jets. However, that's not where he was making the biggest impact. The fact Sanders had 11 receptions for 74 receiving yards speaks to the value he could add to the offense. The rest of the current running back group ― Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel Mc:Laughlin ― have a combined 45 catches for 335 receiving yards. Sanders also leads the team with a 29.3 yards-per-return average on 10 kickoff returns. "It's really in any way possible," Sanders said. "I always had a mindset from a standpoint of whatever they put me, I'm going to try to do my best at. So it's not really from a standpoint of coming back and seeing what I can help them with. It's whatever they feel like I can help them with. So whatever they put me at, just be ready." Sanders is one of three Browns running backs who was on the opening-day active roster, but who missed at least one game due to injury. Sampson also spent five weeks on injured reserve before returning from a Week 1 knee injury, while Judkins also sustained an ankle injury against the Jets that kept him sidelined the next week against the Baltimore Ravens. item.title: Cleveland Guardians Add Lefty Starter on $17.5 Million Deal
item.description: Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images The Cleveland Guardians made their first significant free-agent addition of the winter on Tuesday, agreeing to terms with left-hander Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, according to multiple reports. The deal, which is pending a physical, is the largest one-year guarantee in franchise history and gives Cleveland a familiar AL Central arm to bolster a rotation that already features Parker Messick and Gavin Williams. Bubic, 29, was a 2025 American League All-Star with the Royals, posting a career-best 2.55 ERA over 116⅓ innings that season. His 2026 campaign was far more limited. Elbow and shoulder issues sidelined him for much of the year; he finished with a 3.76 ERA across 55 innings split between Kansas City and the Dodgers after a deadline trade. When healthy, he has shown a five-pitch mix built around a rising four-seam fastball, a firm changeup, and a pair of breaking balls, along with a delivery that has historically generated soft contact and ground balls. For Cleveland, the signing fits a clear priority. The Guardians entered the offseason looking to add starting pitching depth after a season in which they were the only team in baseball to have four pitchers make at least 30 starts. Bubic is expected to slot into the middle of a group that also includes Messick (2026 AL Rookie of the Year and Cy Young finalist), Williams (AL strikeout leader), Tanner Bibee, and several depth options. Outside the Bubic agreement, Cleveland’s offseason activity has been quiet and roster-focused. At the non-tender deadline, they non-tendered utility man David Fry, agreed to deals with relievers Matt Festa and Colin Holderman plus outfielder Blake Perkins to avoid arbitration, and have signed minor-league free agents (including right-hander Jairo Iriarte and left-hander Antoine Kelly). They also added several players to the 40-man roster and claimed José Tena off waivers. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire December 1, the remaining window for additional moves is short . Bubic gives the Guardians an upside left-handed starter on a prove-it deal while they evaluate further pitching or lineup needs.

item.title: Dolphins Rookie Calls Out Bills’ Josh Allen Over Controversial No-Call
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills jogs onto the field before the game against the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) Getty The Miami Dolphins left Buffalo with a loss and a question about how Josh Allen escaped a flag. Rookie cornerback Chris Johnson addressed his clash with the Buffalo Bills quarterback after Sunday’s 26-9 defeat. Allen appeared to grab Johnson’s facemask and throw him to the ground following an interception return in the second quarter. Officials didn’t penalize him. Chris Johnson Questions Josh Allen’s Unpenalized Facemask Play Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 20: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers stiff arms Chris Johnson #3 of the Miami Dolphins in the first quarter of a game at Levi’s Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Johnson made clear he thought the contact crossed a line, even as he said he was ready to move forward. “Definitely surprised there was no flag thrown. Isaiah Smalls II . “Like, I get a little scuffle after the play but I feel like once you get into another player’s helmet or something like that, it’s usually a flag but it is what it is. We move on from it.” Dolphins CB Chris Johnson's reaction to Bills QB Josh Allen using his face mask to slam into him to the ground: "Definitely surprised there was no flag thrown. I feel like when that happens, it's an automatic flag. Like, I get a little scuffle after the play but I feel like once… pic.twitter.com/9CEhhok4YG — c. isaiah smalls ii (@stclaudeii) November 24, 2026 The sequence began with Miami creating a chance to cut into Buffalo’s lead. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez intercepted Allen after edge rusher Chop Robinson deflected the pass, according to the Dolphins’ game recap . Rodriguez returned the interception 26 yards. Johnson’s involvement came as Miami tried to block for its returner, before the exchange with Allen became the focus. Johnson’s complaint centered on the helmet contact. He acknowledged the pushing that can follow a play, but said he expected officials to draw the line when a player grabbed another player’s helmet. His response also stopped short of promising payback or escalating the

item.title: NFL Clears DK Metcalf Of Suspension After Sunday Ejection
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The National Football League has decided against suspending Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf after he was ejected during Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. This ruling comes despite Metcalf committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties that led to his removal from the game late in the third quarter. The league determined that a suspension was not warranted for the incident where Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. While the suspension is off the table, the league will still review the conduct to see if a fine is necessary. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the situation during his Monday media availability, noting that he and Metcalf had spoken about the event. McCarthy described the conversations between the two as “productive” and stated that any further discipline from the team would be kept internal. “Life’s about learning situations,” McCarthy said. He also expressed his belief in second chances, noting that he would judge Metcalf based on their personal interactions rather than just the penalty flags. A History of Discipline This ejection marks the third time in his eight-season career that Metcalf has been thrown out of a game. The final two games of the 2025 regular season carry a suspension for the player due to behavior stemming from a physical altercation with a Lions fan in Detroit. The financial toll on the player has been significant, with his fines totaling a whopping $245,647 according to reports. This total excludes an extra $555,555 fine associated with the two-game suspension resulting from the Lions fan altercation. After Sunday’s game, Metcalf exited the locker room without talking to reporters, though he came back to speak with the media on Monday. ProFootballTalk states that he rejected claims he intended to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. With just one catch on four targets for two yards before ejection, the 28-year-old receiver struggled to find his rhythm this season. In 10 games, the two-time Pro Bowler has secured 36 of his 74 targets, accumulating 434 yards and only two touchdowns. Looking Ahead to Denver Metcalf remains on the Steelers’ active roster as they prepare for their next matchup. The team has a short week to recover before hosting the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. The game is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 27, with kickoff set for 3 p.m. ET. RotoBaller indicates that Metcalf currently sits as the WR40 in half-PPR scoring.

item.title: Dyson Daniels Proves The League Wrong On Value
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Dyson Daniels is the Atlanta Hawks’ most valuable player, not Jalen Johnson, because he drives wins without shooting. Soaring Down South reported that Daniels holds a staggering +18.0 on/off net rating to start the year. This number is the best on the team. The league thinks a shooter is needed to win. Daniels is changing that view with his defense and speed. He impacts winning in every way except shooting, which is a rare skill set. The Thompson twins are the only other players who succeed this way, but both are struggling this season. Amen Thompson has a -9.7 on/off rating with the Rockets, while Ausar sits at +2.2 with the Pistons. Daniels has surpassed both of them. A Deal That Saves The Hawks Money Daniels remains on a team-friendly deal of $25 million per year through the 2029-2030 season. He will have the 35th-highest salary in the league that year, making it the 23rd-lowest contract. Other players in his $20-30 million range include Damian Lillard, Herb Jones, and PJ Washington. Daniels is only 23 years old, one year younger than Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. By the time his contract ends after the 2030 season, he will be 27 and entering his prime. The contract gives the Hawks an advantage over other teams.

item.title: Mahomes And Reid Show Chiefs Pride Supports Kansas City Current
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs did not wait for a press release to show support for their city. Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid made their stance clear on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. While the team prepared for a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, the focus shifted to a family moment that celebrated a local soccer title. Mahomes, dressed in his full uniform, stopped to greet his wife and children. This act of love happened right before kickoff on a cold November afternoon. A Family Moment on the Sideline The video of the reunion spread fast across social media after the league shared it. Mahomes was already in his red No. 15 jersey when he walked over to the sideline. His children were bundled up in warm coats against the chill. One daughter wore a pale pink puffer coat while the other stood close. The quarterback bent down to wrap his arms around both kids for hugs and kisses. He then turned his attention to Brittany Mahomes, who wore a long black coat. She reached up to touch his face before they shared a kiss. The NFL posted the clip on X with a simple note about the moment. They wrote, “@PatrickMahomes getting some pregame love from his favorite people,” according to Sports Illustrated . Fans React to the Tribute Local fans saw the connection between the NFL champion and the NWSL champions immediately. Brittany Mahomes had already shared photos of the Kansas City Current winning their title. Her husband and the head coach supported her, and the community took notice. People watching the feed reacted with warm words about the scene. One person commented, “Okay that hug actually got me,” per Sports Illustrated. Another viewer simply said, “They are adorable.” A third fan summed up the feeling of the day by writing, “pregame with the family hits different.” These comments show how much the city cares about all its teams, not just one. The Chiefs have built a culture that values family and local pride in equal measure. Mahomes and Reid proved that point without saying a word during the game. The team won their match against Arizona with a final score of 34 to 7 on Sunday. Now the squad looks ahead to their next challenge on the road. The Kansas City Chiefs will play the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m.

item.title: Sam Rinzel’s Historic Run Earns Third Star Honor
item.description: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Sam Rinzel has finally gotten the recognition he deserves after a wild week of play. The NHL announced on Monday, Nov. 23, that the young defenseman earned the league’s Third Star of the Week. This marks a massive shift for a player many fans wanted benched just months ago. Rinzel recorded eight points in four games to secure the spot, joining Robert Thomas and Jake Oettinger on the weekly list. According to Blackhawk Up , this achievement makes him the first Blackhawks defenseman to grab this honor since Duncan Keith in December 2013. Rinzel posted 13 points in five games at the end of October, a run that included one goal and 12 assists. He also became only the fourth defenseman in NHL history to record multiple assists in five straight games. That list includes legends like Bobby Orr and Mark Howe. According to Blackhawk Up, his average ice time rose from 16 minutes in October to more than 21 minutes in November. The team trusts him now because he is delivering results on the ice. The first power-play unit he plays on has netted 10 goals across their last six games. The Confidence Shift Teammates and coaches point to one simple reason for this sudden change: confidence. Coach Jeff Blashill noted that the game has finally slowed down for the young defender. Frank Nazar told reporters that Rinzel has been playing with a lot of swagger. “He’s been really confident, playing with a lot of swagger. Him keeping pucks in the zone is a huge part of why he’s succeeding,” Nazar said. Alex Vlasic added that everything Rinzel touches seems to turn into a point lately. The player himself admits he is not overthinking things anymore. Rinzel said, “[I’m] not being afraid to just play — don’t think, just play.” He also noted that he still makes mistakes and has work to do, but the mindset is there. History in the Making Rinzel’s current mindset places him among the best offensive defenders in the league right now. As of Oct. 31, he sat third in the NHL in assists with 14, trailing only Connor McDavid and Kirill Kaprizov. The Blackhawks have gone 4-1-1 in their last six games, and Rinzel has been a huge part of that success. Although his five-game multi-point streak concluded on Sunday versus the Canucks, he performed well and almost recorded additional points. His ability to shoot and create chances has transformed the team’s offense. Regarding his historic run, Rinzel spoke after the game in Calgary, “It definitely wasn’t on my bucket list.” The Blackhawks have found a new leader on their blue line.

item.title: Lakers Target P.J. Washington To Strengthen Frontcourt
item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers are making moves to fix their frontcourt before the trade deadline arrives. General manager Rob Pelinka wants to shore up the team’s depth and add a reliable wing player. Reports indicate the club is targeting Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington to fill a specific hole in their rotation. Heavy.com outlines a specific plan where Dallas sends Washington to Los Angeles in exchange for Jarred Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy, and two future second-round picks. The Mavericks would receive the picks to add assets to their roster while clearing space for other players. This move would reunite Washington with Luka Doncic, his former teammate from Dallas. The Lakers see Washington as the missing piece to help their star trio dominate the playoffs. Why The Lakers Need Washington Los Angeles has struggled to find a consistent two-way player at the forward spot this season. The team needs someone who can guard top scorers and hit open shots without needing the ball. Heavy.com notes that Washington fits this exact profile. Washington is putting up solid numbers this year. While shooting 36.2% from three-point range, he averages 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. Those stats show he can contribute immediately without disrupting the flow of the offense. The Lakers have been linked to him for a long time, but the salary cap makes it difficult. His $88 million contract is a big hurdle, yet the front office seems willing to take the risk. Backup Center Search Continues While chasing Washington, the Lakers are also looking for a backup center to play behind Walker Kessler. Marc Stein reported Sunday that the team is actively seeking help in the middle. “Lakers have been actively searching for another center to play behind Walker Kessler and general manager Rob Pelinka has all but promised that a move is forthcoming to address that need,” Stein wrote. The team has limited draft capital to use as leverage in these talks. One potential target is Mavericks center Moussa Cissé. Rookie guard Walter Clayton Jr. could be added to Dallas’s roster, which might require moving Cissé, and Stein noted that the Lakers have only three tradeable second‑round picks, highlighting their limited draft capital, though Los Angeles could trade Kevon Looney and a pick for Cissé despite the 24‑year‑old logging just 36 minutes this season. He is a gamble on upside rather than a sure thing. The Trade Deadline Approach Rob Pelinka has made it clear that the team plans to be active before the deadline. He spoke on Spectrum SportsNet about the need to fix issues the team has spotted. “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said during a Spectrum SportsNet interview. The front office knows the roster has gaps that need filling if they want to challenge for a championship.

item.title: Guess Who Scored Another OT Goal for the Griffins?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s not much more Grand Rapids Griffins forward John Leonard can do to show how his offensive touch might be able to help the Detroit Red Wings. Leonard scored an overtime goal for a Griffins-record third consecutive game to give the Griffins a 3-2 win against the Manitoba Moose in a Tuesday matinee game. It was his fifth consecutive game-winning goal for Leonard. The New Jersey native, brother of Washington Capitals player Ryan Leonard, showed two goals and an assist in the game. That gives him 13 goals in his past seven games and a league-leading 18 goals in the AHL season. At 28, Leonard is not a true prospect. But the consistency of his scoring — 87 goals in his last 132 AHL games — makes you wonder whether the Red Wings will consider bringing him and playing him with other skilled players. He’s had other call-ups but not really played enough minutes to show what he can do. With the Red Wings struggling offensively, this might be the season to give him an extended shot. John Leonard now boasts 24 game-winning goals over those 132 AHL games. He has a knack of scoring big goals. He leads the league in game-winners (eight) this season Defenseman Axel Sandin-Pellikka and center Nate Danielson registered two assists each to help the Griffins win their seventh consecutive game. Grand Rapids is 17-2-1-1 on the season. Danielson had eight points (2-6–8) in his past four games. Michal Postava made 26 saves to improve his record to 9-0. Carter Bear also scored his sixth goal of the season. item.title: Jiri Lehecka leads Czechs to Davis Cup quarter-final victory over 2022 winners Canada
item.description: Czech No 1 Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4) 6-2 to seal a 2-0 quarter-final victory for Czechia over Canada in the Davis Cup . The world No 14’s victory ensured Czechia booked their place in the last four of tennis’ ‘World Cup’ for the first time in more than a decade. Earlier on Tuesday Tomas Mahac beat Liam Draxl 6-2 3-6 6-2 to put the Czechs in front, with Lehecka’s straightforward win meaning there was no need for the dead-rubber doubles match to be played, with Davis Cup ties best of three. Czechia will now play either three-time defending champions Italy, led by Flavio Cobolli, or South Korea, who face off on Wednesday. The semi-final will take place on Friday. Auger-Aliassime, a former world No 4 now ranked 17th, squandered ​nine ⁠break points, including a set ‌point at 5-4 in the opening set, before Lehecka forced a tiebreak. He continued to keep the Canadian under pressure with his aggressive play and powerful forehand, earning an early break before going 3-0 up in the second set, and converted his second match point before celebrating with his teammates. Lehecka said: “It was a super tough match. I was forced to play very well facing some break points and some tough situations. “Felix is such a dangerous player in these conditions, so I’m very proud with the way I converted the chances I had in the first set and also how I was able to improve my game in the second. I think it’s a great win, not just for me but for the whole team and I’m very, very proud of the team.” Earlier Machac, the mixed doubles champion from the 2024 Paris Olympics, made a flying start against world No 154 Draxl, surging into a 4-0 lead in ‌the first set. But what had looked like an easy win for the Czech turned into a real battle as Draxl fought back to force a decider. Machac regained control by breaking ‌for a 4-2 lead ​in the third before sealing ‌victory in an hour and 55 minutes.

item.title: How Tinubu saved Buhari from disqualification in 2015 election — Omatseye
item.description: — No conspiracy will stop President’s re-election — Tinubu was kept at a distance in Buhari’s administration — Osoba By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Former President Muhammadu Buhari could have been disqualified from the 2015 presidential election had Bola Tinubu, then APC national leader, not urgently called eminent lawyer Wole Olanipekun. This was disclosed by veteran journalist Sam Omatseye in Chapter 29, pages 483–485, of his book, From AD to APC: The Evolution of Nigerian Political Parties and the Exploits of One Man (1998–2015), which was launched yesterday by President Tinubu at the Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. This is as former Governor of Ogun State and veteran journalist, Aremu Segun Osoba, stated that after helping to put in place the All Progressives Congress government led by the late Muhammadu Buhari, President Tinubu was kept at a distance by the administration. An excerpt of Tinubu’s intervention to ensure that Buhari was on the ballot in 2015 was contained in the programme of events for the book’s public presentation, attended by several governors. According to the book, days before the 2015 presidential election, Tinubu phoned Olanipekun, asking him to rush to the Federal High Court in Abuja or Buhari might not contest the poll. Olanipekun was in Akure, Ondo State, on an official assignment on a Monday evening, a few days before the March 28, 2015 election, when Tinubu called him. Olanipekun narrated in the book: “I was in Akure, Ondo State, on an official assignment on the fateful Monday evening when I got a call from Asiwaju. “And as usual, I was trying to embark on the usual exchange of banter and pleasantries by hailing him as my Asiwaju of the universe.” However, his humour was deflected due to the gravity of the challenge on the ground. “He sharply replied that there is fire on the mountain and you’re shouting Asiwaju of the universe; there’s an emergency here, where are you?” Tinubu was quoted as saying. Olanipekun said he told Tinubu that the assignment would last until the following day. Tinubu then raised his voice and told him: “You have to leave that your Akure immediately as your attention and presence are imperative at the Federal High Court in Abuja tomorrow, otherwise Buhari might not contest the election coming up this Saturday.” Although the excerpt did not state the case before the court, several suits before the Federal High Court in Abuja sought to disqualify Buhari from the March 28, 2015 presidential election, in what became known as the certificate saga. The plaintiffs argued that Buhari did not submit his academic certificates with his Form CF001 to the Independent National Electoral Commission. They said this breached Sections 131 and 318 of the 1999 Constitution and Section 31(3) of the Electoral Act, 2010. One plaintiff, Chike Okafor, accused Buhari of perjury and asked the court to restrain INEC from allowing him to take part in the election. The suits were heard before Justice Adeniyi Ade
