item.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
item.description: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math, a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows on several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by Large Language Model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, "It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field." Read full article Comments

item.title: UK police arrest two men after break-in at William and Kate’s home
item.description: Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said on Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the countryside retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine, who were not in residence at the time. Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England, after the local force received a call just before 6:00 pm (1800 GMT) on Monday of “suspicious activity”, Norfolk police said in a statement sent to AFP. Anmer Hall where William, Kate and their three children occasionally live — especially during the school holidays — was broken into, according to UK media. The 10-bedroom red-brick Georgian manor was gifted to the couple by the late Queen Elizabeth II after their marriage. The men “were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass”, police said. The sprawling Sandringham estate is owned by William’s father King Charles III. Police said the property “was unoccupied” at the time and the men remained in custody. William and Kate mainly live at their home on the Windsor estate, just west of London. Kensington Palace, which handles the affairs of William, the heir to the throne, told AFP they would not comment on security matters. Charles’s disgraced brother, the former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, moved to Sandringham earlier this year and lives about a mile from Anmer Hall. The king ousted Andrew from his home of two decades in Windsor and stripped him of his royal titles amid the fallout from his brother’s alleged dealings with the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. – Chat with the queen – It is not the first time a royal residence has been broken into, despite the tight security surrounding the royal family. In 2024, several intruders were caught on the Windsor estate after they broke into a farm building and tried to steal a pick-up truck and a quad bike. Around Christmas 2021, a 21-year-old man with mental health issues was arrested after being caught near the queen’s apartments armed with a loaded crossbow. He admitted in court to trying to kill Elizabeth and was handed a nine-year sentence, to be served initially in the high-security Broadmoor psychiatric hospital. The most famous incident was in July 1982, when a man named Michael Fagan sneaked into Buckingham Palace and made his way to Queen Elizabeth II’s bedroom. He sat on her four-poster bed and had a 10-minute chat with her before being taken away by security. He was initially charged but the accusations were later dropped. News of Monday’s break-in came just as William made his first visit to Downing Street for talks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The two men discussed their “shared commitment to tackling the earth’s greatest challenges,” a Downing Street spokesperson said. “They turned to homelessness and their shared desire to find sustainable options for prevention, followed by defence and security issues and the Commonwealth,” the spokesperson added. item.title: TikTok was down
item.description: Earlier on Tuesday, TikTok experienced some issues, with videos, search results, favorites, and other features not loading as they usually do. Videos sometimes wouldn't load in the For You feed on my iPhone, and search results occasionally didn't show up as expected in the app on iOS or Android, or on the web. Even trying to pull up a profile would show a blank page, while links to videos are dead in the water too. However, as of 3:45PM ET or so, things appear to be working normally again. item.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
item.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

item.title: Campaign violence: INEC awaits police case files to prosecute offenders
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has asked the Nigeria Police Force to speed up the arrest, investigation and transmission of case files against perpetrators of campaign violence, so the Commission can prosecute them directly. The INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, said swift action was necessary so that “impunity is decisively checked before January.” He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the Inspector General of Police’s Interactive Session with Chairmen and Secretaries of Political Parties on a peaceful electoral process before, during and after the 2027 General Elections. The session held at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peace Conference Hall, Force Headquarters. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had “significantly strengthened legal deterrence,” adding that Sections 96 and 97 prohibit inciting campaign rhetoric and ban the use of thugs, private armed guards or masquerades at political rallies. According to him, the Act prescribes penalties of up to ₦5 million or twelve months’ imprisonment for individuals, and up to ₦10 million for political parties, on initial breaches. “Under Section 148, INEC is empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receipt of completed case files,” he said, explaining the Commission’s request for prompt transmission of the files by the Police. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other federal security agencies. Amupitan reminded political parties that INEC Guidelines require them to notify the Commissioner of Police in writing of rally venues and times, and to submit the details to the Commission at least ten days in advance. He appealed to political leaders “to refrain from seeking political support by creating fear,” urging them instead to “earn public confidence through integrity and transparency.” The Chairman said the nation was at “a decisive moment” on its democratic calendar. The Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold in 53 days, on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 176,846 polling units. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will follow on Saturday, February 6, 2027. He also asked for targeted police coverage of designated mock polling centres and collation points nationwide for the Commission’s mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026. According to him, the exercise will span all 36 states and the FCT. It will test

item.title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
item.description: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

item.title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State. The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State. It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections. The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.” It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’ The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement. It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern. The MDPCO accused the APC leadership of failing to take decisive action against members allegedly involved in political violence, warning that its silence could further embolden those responsible. “This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition,” it said. The organisation warned that Nigerians would not accept the use of violence or insecurity as instruments of electoral conquest, insisting that political parties must respect citizens’ freedom to choose their leaders. It declared that the resort to violence would not alter what it described as Nigerians’ determination to vote the APC out of power. “The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said. It demanded an immediate end to what it described as attempts to suppress democratic participation, while urging Nigerians to support its principal, Engr. Seyi Makinde

item.title: It was reprisal action – Ughelli LG chairman accuses Omo-Agege’s boys of firing first shot
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Movudu Egbo, has described the violence involving Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and his supporters as a reprisal, accusing the senator’s men of killing community members before the incident escalated. Egbo, who had earlier been accused by Omo-Agege of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt on the senator, denied the allegation, claiming that the violence was triggered by the killing of the community’s president-general and other residents. Speaking on Channels Television on Tuesday, the council chairman alleged that Omo-Agege’s supporters fired the first shots, killing members of the community where the senator held his campaign rally. He said the incident was a sad development, extending condolences to victims on both sides of the violence, regardless of their political affiliations. “Let me express my sincere condolences to all those who lost their lives yesterday on both sides. Most of them know to me. They are my friends. Whether they are working for NDC or APC, nobody’s life is worth the ambition of anybody, and it was a sad day yesterday,” he said. Egbo alleged that Omo-Agege had made provocative remarks against him during his campaign visit to the community, claiming that the senator allegedly incited his supporters before they opened fire. He said he was not present at the venue when the campaign took place, as he was in his office, but alleged that Omo-Agege abused him while addressing residents and subsequently riled up his supporters. “But when he was leaving, he riled up the people. He gave instructions to his boys, and then they gunned down the president-general of the community and then shut other people down. It was that death that brought that anger,” Egbo alleged. The council chairman described the subsequent violence as a reprisal for the killing, claiming that the community was angered by the death of its leader and other innocent residents. “What happened yesterday was a reprisal action to answer to the unjust killing of the president and two other onlookers who were innocent,” he said. Reacting to Omo-Agege’s claim that he was targeted for assassination, Egbo questioned the presence of firearms at the senator’s campaign rally, alleging that his supporters were armed. “At the end of it all, he came to TV and was saying that they wanted to kill him. You don’t go to campaign rallies with AK-47. You don’t go to campaign rallies with pump-action rifles. What are you going to use them for?” he asked. Egbo further questioned why supporters attending a political rally would be carrying weapons, alleging that the firearms were used against members of the community. “The people that are going to vote for you, you want to kill them?” he said. His allegations come amid conflicting accounts of the violence, with Omo-Agege accusing Egbo of orchestrating an assassination attempt against him during his campaign visit to Delta community. item.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
item.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. (2026)) The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower

item.title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The event attracted supporters from the 14 local government areas of the state, including party faithful, women and youth groups, traditional leaders and other political stakeholders. Addressing the gathering, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said voting for the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the state Houses of Assembly, would enable the state to benefit from federal government projects, appointments and other interventions. He argued that Zamfara could not afford to remain in opposition in 2027, urging residents to align with the ruling party at the federal level. “I urge you, the good people of Zamfara, to vote for APC from top to bottom in 2027. Vote for President Tinubu, vote for Governor Lawal, vote for our senators, House of Representatives members and State Assembly members. That is the only way Zamfara will move forward,” Yari said. He also urged voters to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the President as the candidate capable of driving development in the North-West and the country. Yari said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated commitment to addressing insecurity, reviving the economy, improving infrastructure and repositioning the country for sustainable growth. He noted that the North-West, which had experienced years of banditry, kidnapping and economic challenges, needed sustained investment in security and development. “President Tinubu is the only candidate who, if given a second mandate, will develop the North-West and the country at large. He has the vision, the experience and the political will to take Nigeria to the next level. We must give him our full support,” he said. Yari called on Zamfara residents to give Tinubu substantial electoral support in 2027, as they did in 2023, to enable him to complete his reform agenda. He also canvassed support for Governor Lawal’s second-term ambition, saying the governor needed the backing of residents to consolidate his administration’s Rescue Zamfara Agenda. According to him, cooperation between the Federal Government and the Zamfara State Government would accelerate development in security, job creation, education, healthcare and infrastructure. The campaign launch was attended by APC stakeholders, government officials, members of the state executive council, federal and state lawmakers, local government chairmen, women and youth groups, and party supporters. item.title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat. The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area. Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed. The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations. The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North. Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party. “The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none. “We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.” He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled. The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements. Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex. He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas. The post 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PSC appoints CP Usman Adamu Zamfara Police Commissioner
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State. The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections. According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety. Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police. The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani. item.title: Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins. From custodian to full-service bank Founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025. The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks. item.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
item.description: The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday. CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028. The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final. The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year. “The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.” The host cities and other details will be announced later. “We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani. “We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.” The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling that restored Senegal’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title following its dispute with Morocco. CAF made its position known in a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, saying it respected the decision of the Lausanne based tribunal and would take the necessary steps to give effect to it. “CAF respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it,” the football governing body said. The CAS ruling overturned the CAF Appeal Board’s decision of March 17, 2026, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after ruling that the Teranga Lions had forfeited the final. Instead, the tribunal reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board, which had upheld Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the final played in Rabat on January 18, 2026. The dispute followed a controversial incident late in regulation time when Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty. The Senegalese players returned after about 14 minutes, but Morocco captain Brahim Diaz failed to convert the spot kick. Senegal later secured victory through Pape Gueye’s goal in extra time. Morocco subsequently challenged the result, arguing that Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which address situations where a team abandons or refuses to continue a match. However, CAS ruled that the provisions did not apply because the referee had not permanently abandoned the match. The tribunal also held that the referee acted within his authority when he allowed play to resume. The decision was unanimous, according to CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb, who said the panel found no legal error in the referee’s handling of the incident. The tribunal’s ruling does not affect separate disciplinary sanctions imposed by CAF on Senegal coach Pape Thiaw and players Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr over incidents during the final. Although CAF has promised to comply with the decision, it has not yet provided details of the administrative steps or a timeline for implementing the ruling. CAS confirmed that the full grounds for its decision had been communicated to the parties on Tuesday. The award is expected to be made public in due course, unless the parties request that it remain confidential. The ruling brings an end to the dispute over the final and restores Senegal’s second AFCON title, following its first triumph in 2021. The post CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. The post ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
item.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. item.title: Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in the Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area of the state. The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, was arrested following reports of repeated grave desecration at the cemetery. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the arrest followed a surveillance operation mounted by the police in collaboration with concerned youths in the community. According to him, on November 10, 2026, at about 7:15 p.m., shortly after the burial of a deceased person, the suspect was allegedly caught digging into the newly covered grave. Usman said vigilant youths apprehended him while he was allegedly committing the act and immediately alerted the police. He added that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons. The police spokesman further said the suspect reportedly admitted involvement in previous acts of grave desecration at the same cemetery, including an earlier incident in which he allegedly removed and took away the burial shroud of a deceased person. Usman said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action. The command commended members of the community for their vigilance and cooperation, while cautioning residents against taking the law into their own hands. It urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities to the police. The post Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, life jackets and other water safety equipment to riverine communities in Bayelsa State following a deadly boat mishap. The House also urged relevant agencies to intensify rescue operations, provide relief materials to affected communities and investigate the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Rodney Ebikebina Ambaiowei, representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, during plenary on Tuesday. Ambaiowei told the House that more than 150 people, mostly indigenes of Southern Ijaw, were involved in the accident on November 20, 2026, while travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a condolence visit. He said the boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan, throwing its occupants into the water. According to him, rescue efforts began immediately, with the Bayelsa State Government, security personnel and other relevant agencies responding to the incident. He disclosed that, as of November 22, several people had been rescued alive with varying degrees of injuries and discomfort, while others had died. The rescued victims, he said, were taken to medical facilities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area and government hospitals in Yenagoa for treatment, while search and rescue operations continued for missing persons and possible survivors. The lawmaker expressed concern that several victims were still missing, despite the efforts of the state government, and called for a broader search operation. He said the tragedy had plunged families and residents of Southern Ijaw, particularly Ukubie and neighbouring communities, into mourning. Ambaiowei attributed the vulnerability of riverine communities partly to the poor condition of boats used for transportation, noting that many were old, overworked and overloaded because of the scarcity of vessels. He also lamented the absence of life jackets, floaters and other water safety equipment, as well as inadequate enforcement of their use, despite waterways being the major means of transportation in the largely riverine constituency. The lawmaker said the communities had limited access to motorable roads, despite ongoing road construction efforts by the Bayelsa State Government, leaving residents heavily dependent on waterways. He warned that failure by the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant bodies to intensify rescue operations and provide relief materials could worsen the impact of the tragedy. Ambaiowei added that the affected communities depended largely on fishing for food and income, stressing that the accident had disrupted their livelihoods and economic activities. He commended President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the affected area to sympathise with families of the deceased. The lawmaker also acknowledged the Federal Government’s donation of ₦25

item.title: Bingo on a Global Scale
item.description: Bingo might seem like a fairly simple game, but it’s played in all sorts of different ways around the world. The basic idea is usually the same: match the numbers as they’re called and hope to complete your card before everyone else. But the rules, formats and even the way people play can vary quite a bit depending on where you are. Online bingo has made things even more interesting. Players aren’t restricted to their local halls anymore, and there are plenty of different versions to try without leaving the house. Different Games for Different Tastes Ideally, everyone’s favourite online bingo site would have all the games to cater to all tastes. That means bigger prizes, more games to discover and plenty of social interaction with players from all over the world. And there’s certainly no shortage of choice. In the UK, 90-ball bingo is the traditional favourite. Cards have three rows and nine columns, with players looking to complete one line, two lines or a full house. It’s the format most people associate with a classic bingo night. Across the Atlantic, things are a little different. American bingo usually uses 75 balls and a five-by-five card, with players trying to complete particular patterns. These can include straight lines, diagonals, corners or more complicated shapes. Then there’s 80-ball bingo, which has become popular online. It uses a four-by-four card and offers a middle ground between the British and American formats. It’s quick, straightforward and gives developers plenty of room to come up with different patterns. The Rules Depend on Where You Play Legislation is another area where things can change considerably. In the UK, online bingo operators need a licence from the Gambling Commission and follow rules covering player protection, advertising, identity checks and responsible gambling. There are also specific requirements around how games are operated and how customer funds are handled. Canada takes a different approach with gambling regulation being largely a provincial matter, so the rules depend on where players are located. Ontario has its regulated iGaming market, while Alberta introduced its own licensed online gambling framework in 2026. In the US, it gets even more convoluted. While some states allow online bingo or gambling, others impose stricter laws. The operators need to be aware of local laws instead of assuming that a license in one state will automatically give them the authority to run a gambling operation in any other state. Europe is just as varied. Countries such as Sweden, Spain and Germany have their own licensing systems and requirements. So a bingo site operating in several European markets may need to meet quite different standards. More Than Just Calling Numbers The social aspect of bingo contributes almost as much to its attractiveness as the game itself. item.title: Benue APC crisis: Why Alia/Akume reconciliation ‘ll not work – Agada
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Factional Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Benue State, Mr Austin Agada, has declared that there is currently no genuine reconciliation between the camps of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume, and Governor Hyacinth Alia, insisting that any peace deal must go beyond preparations for the 2027 general elections. Agada, an ally of Senator Akume, made the position known in a social media exchange with another APC stalwart and Akume loyalist, Mr Abua Yaji, where he explained why previous reconciliation efforts within the ruling party in the state had failed. He maintained that reconciliation could only be meaningful if it addressed the broader concerns of the Benue people, stressing that it must not be reduced to an arrangement designed to secure political advantage ahead of the next elections. According to him, “the truth remains that reconciliation cannot be done on the basis of electioneering alone. If there must be reconciliation in the first place, it has to be genuine, and it will not even be with us, it will be with the Benue people.” Agada recalled the massive support the APC enjoyed from the electorate during the 2023 general elections, arguing that any reconciliation process must take into consideration the expectations and interests of the people who voted for the party. “Reconciliation must be seen to be total in all spheres, considering the level the Benue people came out in the last election in 2023 to vote for our party under my leadership. So, when they are ready for reconciliation, we will know. But for now, there is no reconciliation; they are not ready for reconciliation,” he declared. He, however, clarified that his position did not amount to a rejection of dialogue among party leaders, noting that there was nothing wrong with political stakeholders sitting together to resolve their differences. “The Benue people have their resolve already, it does not matter what anybody thinks about it. But the truth about it is that there is nothing wrong for people to sit down and talk. We are not in a theatre of war. Even in a war situation, people sit down and talk,” he said. Explaining further, Agada described the ongoing engagements among the party leaders as brotherly discussions, insisting that any eventual agreement must be transparent and acceptable to the people of the state. “So, what is going on is that they are talking as brothers, and if it reaches the time for a genuine reconciliation, the entire Benue people will know. People will sit down and people will speak out,” he stated. He stressed that the disagreement within the APC should not be viewed as a personal contest involving Akume or any other political leader, but as an issue concerning the entire party structure and the people of Benue state. “So, it is not about Austin Agada or the SGF, George Akume. It is about the Benue people and the entire leadership of our party from the ward level to the

item.title: Arm strongarms site that hosts ad-free documentation and it may disappear
item.description: Arm is swinging the hammer at an enthusiast’s site hosting a bloat-free version of its instruction reference documentation, demanding it be taken offline after several years of availability. The demand from Arm lawyers to Jon Palmisciano concern Jon’s Arm Reference , a site that provides the same arm Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) info available on Arm’s site, but with what Palmisciano describes as “without a million popups and all of the bloat” that Arm provides on its own. According to Palmisciano, his copy of the Arm ISA was culled from machine-readable XML files and stripped of the bloat. He built his version in 2022 with new CSS on top of it, and the addition of a quick search feature that, according to his comments on Hacker News, isn’t available in the official version. “The aim has always been to make it the most comfortable and bullshit-free browsing experience for people who need these docs daily,” Palmisciano wrote in HN. Based on the responses the site seems to have plenty of fans. That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture. Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else. As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form. “Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Palmisciano told us. That said, Palmisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Palmisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page. “I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Palmisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen. Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Palmisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation. "We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. The post Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
item.description: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability. item.title: Best New Nigerian Songs This Week: Rema, Wizkid, Falz, Simi & More
item.description: Falz and Simi reunite on their new single “Jaiye”, ten years after their 2016 joint EP Chemistry. Photo Credit: Falz/Instagram Your playlist called, it wants a proper refresh before the week runs away from you. Between surprise link-ups from two of Afrobeats’ biggest names, cheeky big-money banter, and easy-going tunes built for the dance floor, Nigerian artists have given us plenty to queue up right now. If you are hunting for something smooth to soundtrack your Lagos traffic commute, gearing up for a night out, or simply tired of hitting replay on the same ten tracks, here are five new Nigerian songs to listen to this week that deserve a spot in your rotation. Rema featuring Wizkid – “Feel Alright” When Rema and Wizkid finally lock into the studio together, you press play immediately. Serving as the opening track on Rema’s freshly released seven-track EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB )—which follows his 2024 album HEIS and 2023’s Ravage EP—”Feel Alright” brings two generations of global Afrobeats stars onto one mid-tempo groove. Rema glides across the beat in a mix of English, Pidgin, and Yoruba while pursuing a love interest, before Wizkid slides in with his laid-back cadence. The official lyric video is already out too, so you can catch every bar from start to finish. ﻿ Adekunle Gold featuring Blaqbonez – “Money in a Wheelbarrow” Did you ever picture Adekunle Gold and Blaqbonez on the same track? Adekunle Gold revealed that this single actually reunites him with an artist who dropped a diss track about him years ago—and marks their second attempt at making a song together. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership. item.title: ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region. Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and flag-off of special intervention projects by the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) in Borno State. He recalled that Tinubu played a significant role in securing the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket for former President Muhammadu Buhari ahead of the 2015 general election. According to the vice president, Tinubu deliberately moved the party’s presidential primary to Lagos and mobilised support for Buhari in the South-West, contributing to his emergence as the party’s candidate. “Those of us that were active in the political scene can bear testimony to the fact that without the efforts of President Bola Tinubu, Muhammadu Buhari couldn’t have clinched the ticket of the APC in 2014 in Lagos. “He deliberately shifted the base of the primaries to Lagos, and he worked assiduously to deliver the South-West. And one good turn always deserves another,” Shettima said. ﻿ The vice president urged the people of the North to reciprocate Tinubu’s political support by backing his re-election, declaring that the region had an opportunity to return the favour. “And for us in the North, this is payback time. I urge you, I beseech all of us here, let us use our informed judgment and make decisions that are in the best interest of our nation,” he said. Making a case for the administration’s economic policies, Shettima urged Nigerians to consider the government’s economic performance when deciding who to support in the 2027 elections. He cited a decline in headline inflation and an increase in the country’s foreign reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 17 years. “The economy has turned the corner. Headline inflation has come down. Our foreign reserve is the highest in the past 17 years. It’s now hovering in the region of 55 billion dollars,” he said. Defending the removal of the petrol subsidy, the vice president maintained that the decision was not intended to worsen the economic hardship faced by Nigerians but to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing. “And the President has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy not to inflict pain on Nigerians, no. He removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. The post ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: An AI coding agent, a browser, and a Mac tool found a financial firm's access key in under 6 minutes
item.description: A Romanian hacker, armed with only an open source coding agent, a Chrome browser, and a Mac, tried multiple ways to break into a financial services firm, ultimately found an access key - luckily, it was a decoy - and carried out an entire (almost) attack in under six minutes. It’s a stark reminder that miscreants don’t need sophisticated malware - as in the Binance heist - or AI pen-testing tools like ARTEX to carry out intrusions into critical networks. Open source coding agents, and specifically OpenCode in this case, also work just fine. “What surprised me most was how little it took and the toolkit: a free coding agent, the curl that comes with every Mac and an ordinary Chrome, all from one laptop,” Jesta co-founder and CTO Lior Finkelshtein told The Register . “Until now I thought that we had more time until tools like OpenCode are used in offensive operations. This incident shows us that it's already in use in the field, and we will probably see more of that in the future.” Jesta is a Tel Aviv-based security startup that builds defensive tools to detect and stop autonomous AI attacks. In a report shared exclusively with The Register , Finkelshtein documented an attempted intrusion targeting a major financial services company that’s also a Jesta customer - the security shop declined to say which one. Jesta’s investigation into the incident determined that someone in Bucharest downloaded a free AI coding agent called OpenCode and pointed it at the financial services customer on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET. 'Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking' OpenCode is an open source coding agent that lets users connect to more than 200 model providers or local models, including Anthropic’s Claude models, OpenAI’s GPTs, Google’s Gemini, DeepSeek, and Z.ai’s GLM. Jesta doesn’t know which model the attacker used, as there was nothing in the traffic that named the model. OpenCode's web fetch tool, however, did name itself, so Jesta knows the attacker used this coding agent - not a scanner - to do the dirty work. “Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking,” Finkelshtein said in a Tuesday report about the agent-led attack. But, he added, nothing in the coding agent “stops you from pointing it at someone else's website either. When you do, the agent goes through the site the same way it goes through code. It reads, tries something, reads the result and tries the next thing, for as long as you let it run.” That’s what it did in this operation, which took less than six minutes and cost the human operator nothing. The first call came from a Chrome browser on a Mac, requesting the front page of one of the financial firm’s systems. The site refused it, and six seconds later, the same IPv6 address in Bucharest, on an ordinary DIGI Romania business line, tried again. It used the same Chrome version, but said it was an Android Pixel 10 phone (it wasn’t) to see if the site would let a phone in (it didn’t). After failing to gain access through the front page, the

item.title: Microsoft refreshes Copilot app search for users without an AI subscription
item.description: Microsoft is updating search in its Microsoft 365 Copilot app for users without a Copilot license, with a toggle to restore the classic interface. Google, meanwhile, is giving AI searches more prominence on its homepage, where the familiar Search button is absent from a newly demonstrated layout. Microsoft's change is rolling out now and will hit Deferred Release by mid-January 2027. It will impact users with a Microsoft 365 license who do not have a Copilot license and "provides modern search controls to help users find, refine, and navigate search results more easily." It's enabled by default, which is a shame since administrators would likely prefer an opt-in rather than opt-out approach, and users can switch back to the "classic search experience" via a toggle on the search results page. Microsoft has not specified how long this toggle will remain available. Its separate Copilot Search experience had a fallback toggle scheduled for removal 60 days after general availability. "With the updated search experience, users can continue to find files using keywords, use modern search controls to refine and navigate results, and search supported connected third-party content when their organization has configured connected sources," Microsoft said. The results will still only display content to which users have permission. Microsoft advises administrators to brief users and help desks on the changed interface and the option to switch back. Microsoft's search tweaks arrive as the future of the Google Search button on Google's desktop homepage looks uncertain. In a post , Google VP of Product Robby Stein described a collapsible sidebar that lists users' recent AI conversations, pushing AI deeper into the search experience. Stein called it "a much simpler way to pick up where you left off," and said it would help customers "easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches." However, something else was obvious in Stein's post: the Google Search button was not present. Stein explained in August that Google had performed a "small test on desktop to help people find new things they can do with Search." Part of that test was the removal of the Google Search button. Users can still submit queries by pressing Enter. Stein said the test would have "no impact to how the core search works." The sidebar rollout doesn't itself confirm the Search button's permanent retirement. For now, its absence from Stein's demonstration is another sign of which features Google wants users to notice. ®

item.title: Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real
item.description: Porsche provided flights from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 718 EV prototype. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. It wasn't until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche's upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle. That's not particularly low for a sports car, but it's practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that's usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed. So, for the company's first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance. item.title: Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The company’s blog post cites 236 accounts. Because Coldcard is self-custodial, Coinkite can only count losses that customers report, and it says the true number is likely higher. The report cites Galaxy Research figures showing 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, worth about $107 million at today’s price. Galaxy pegged losses above $115 million in August, based on prices when the coins were taken, and white hats later moved some exposed coins into a recovery trust. Who found and exploited the flaw is still unknown, and law enforcement is investigating. The report calls AI

item.title: Stacks Opens Bond 4 With 1,050 BTC of Bitcoin Staking Capacity
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Stacks Opens Bond 4 With 1,050 BTC of Bitcoin Staking Capacity GRAND CAYMAN, Cayman Islands, Nov. 24, 2026. Stacks Labs today announced 1,050 BTC of capacity for Bond 4 of Bitcoin staking with Stacks, a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. The bond starts ~Dec. 5, and institutions can register at stacks.co/institutional-bitcoin-staking. Bond 4 carries a 3% target annual yield, paid in BTC weekly over a six-month term. Each BTC staked is paired with STX worth 5% of its value, so filling Bond 4’s 1,050 BTC of capacity requires a corresponding STX commitment. Rewards come from Stacks miners, who commit BTC through Proof of Transfer (PoX), the consensus mechanism Stacks has run since January 2021. Every bond since the Genesis Bond launched in September has filled. 21shares returned for Bond 3, and Bullish (NYSE: BLSH) joined as the first top-10 public Bitcoin treasury company to stake BTC. “Opening more than 1,000 BTC of new capacity for institutions shows how strong the demand for Bitcoin yield has become,” said Muneeb Ali, CEO, Stacks Labs, and founder of Stacks. Institutions can stake from qualified custody, including BitGo. During the bootstrap phase, self-custodial Bitcoin staking is whitelisted. Holders who are not on the whitelist can take part through pooled Bitcoin staking at stacks.co/bitcoin-staking . About Stacks Stacks is a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. With Bitcoin staking, holders stake BTC with STX, and their BTC stays on the Bitcoin L1 under their own custody. Stacks has distributed over 4,200 BTC in rewards to participants since 2021. Learn more at stacks.co .
